backend.gatewayPrefix: /api/dev-option — confirmed directly from the Swagger URL the user pasted (http://172.16.0.12/api/dev-option/swagger), not a guessed operationId decode.
backend.responseEnvelope: { success: boolean, message: string, data: object } on every endpoint (health included) — unwrapped in schedulerService.js via a local `unwrap()` helper, same pattern as logsService.js/timeseriesService.js/documentsService.js.
backend.authHeadersActuallySent: Authorization: Bearer <token> AND Cookie: access_token=<token> — injected globally by the proxy factory (createProxy), never per-route.
backend.priorState: This feature previously existed as a UI-first stub with NO real backend: SERVICE_DEVELOPER_OPTIONS_URL was unset, and the service (schedulerService.js) called a placeholder contract (/scheduler/jobs GET+POST, /scheduler/restart POST, body field `cron_schedule`). That entire stub contract was deleted and replaced by the real one below once the user supplied the live Swagger endpoint table + real response samples (2026-07-27).

decisions.question: Are schedules plant-scoped (Rule 0) or system-level (as the old stub's comment claimed)?
decisions.answer: Plant-scoped. Every schedule object in the real GET /schedule and GET /schedule/{id} response samples carries a `plant_code_id` field (e.g. "Plant_1"), and the /reload response also echoes `plant_code_id` back — this directly contradicts the old stub's assumption. plant_code_id is now sent on every endpoint except /health per Rule 0 (body for POST/PUT, query for GET/DELETE), sourced from useApp().plantCode in useScheduler.js.

decisions.question: The user's create/update request body samples don't show a plant_code_id field at all (only job_name, cron_expression, method, url, payload, headers) — does this mean create/update really don't need it?
decisions.answer: LIVE-CONFIRMED (2026-07-27) the doc's omission was real signal, not an incomplete example: POST /schedule 422'd with {success:false, message:"Validation failed", errors:[{field:"plant_code_id", message:"Field required"}]} even though the body already contained plant_code_id — this app-level error shape has no `loc`, but the only explanation consistent with a body field that IS present yet still reported missing is that the endpoint's Pydantic model declares plant_code_id as a Query() param instead, same mismatch class as symbolic-ai's multipart endpoints (see CLAUDE.md). Fixed: createSchedule/updateSchedule now send plant_code_id as a query param (kept in the body too, harmless). Flag to backend/product if PUT /schedule/{id} turns out to need the same fix confirmed live (only POST has been live-tested so far).

decisions.question: Does /schedule/{id}/enable and /disable take a body?
decisions.answer: No sample body shown for either in the doc (both marked NA) and both are simple state-toggle actions — implemented as bodyless POSTs with plant_code_id as a query param instead, consistent with the GET/DELETE query-param convention. UNCONFIRMED — no live test yet.

notes: GET /health does NOT carry plant_code_id — it reports the scheduler process's own run-state ({scheduler_running: boolean}), not plant data, so it is the one endpoint deliberately exempted from Rule 0.

cron_expression sample data is inconsistent: two of three sample schedules use a standard 5-field cron ("*/5 * * * *", "* * * * *") but one uses 6 fields with a leading seconds column ("0 */1 * * * *"). The existing 5-field validator (_lib/cron.js) and edit-form splitter (ScheduleFormModal.jsx's splitCron) both assume 5 fields and fall back to defaults if a schedule's cron_expression doesn't split into exactly 5 parts, rather than guessing which field is seconds vs minute. Flag to backend if 6-field (seconds-precision) cron is actually a supported/intended format.
This migration also renamed the request field cron_schedule (old stub) -> cron_expression (real contract) and the endpoint job_name stayed the same.
